page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Bond length and bond angle
lines: between the nuclei of two bonded atoms in
Bond angle: the angle between the orbitals
Ex: the H−O−H bond angle in water is 104.5°.
steps.why: Both parameters describe geometry: length fixes how far apart two bonded nuclei sit, angle fixes the direction of one bond against another at the same atom.
common_mistakes: Measuring bond length between electron clouds. It is nucleus to nucleus.
Leaving out equilibrium — the atoms vibrate about this distance.
steps.memory_tip: Length is nucleus to nucleus; angle is bond direction against bond direction.
steps.margin_note: One definition per line, each with its measuring points named.

steps.label: Bond enthalpy

lines.text: Bond enthalpy: energy to break one mole of a bond

lines: The energy required to break one mole of
bonds of a particular type between two
Its unit is kJ mol⁻¹. A larger bond
steps.why: Bond enthalpy is the strength parameter of the set: it measures the bond's strength as an energy, and the gaseous-state condition keeps other interactions out of the measurement.
common_mistakes: Leaving out one mole or gaseous state — both are part of the definition.
Writing the unit as kJ. It is kJ per mole: kJ mol⁻¹.
steps.memory_tip: One mole, gas phase, energy in — the three pieces of the definition.
steps.margin_note: Close with the unit; it is asked with the definition.

insider_note: Three terms but only two marks, so bond length and bond angle share one and get a line each with no padding. Bond enthalpy has a mark to itself and must carry one mole, the gaseous state and its unit.
